questions.q: The area of the region enclosed between the parabolas $y^{2} = 2x - 1$~and $y^{2} = 4x - 3$ is.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$We have,& $y^{2} = 2x - 1 . . . \left(1\right)$~and $y^{2} = 4x - 3 . . . \left(2\right)$

We first find the points of intersection of the given parabolas by solving the~equations \left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$simultaneously.

This gives,~$2x - 1 = 4x - 3$

$⇒ 2x = 2⇒ x = 1$

Now, put $x = 1$~in equation~ \left(1\right)$,~we get~$y = \pm1$.

Now, the equations~ \left($1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ can be written as

$y^{2} = 2 \left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$y^{2} = 4 \left($x - $\dfrac{3}{4}\right)~respectively.

The graphs of these two curves are shown in figure.

We have to find the area of the shaded region.

Now, the equations \left(1\right) & \left(2\right)$~can be written as

$x = \dfrac{y^{2} + 1}{2}$~&~$x = \dfrac{y^{2} + 3}{4}$~respectively.

It is clear from the figure,~required area $A = 2{∫}_{0}^{1}\left({x}_{2} - {x}_{1}\right)dy$~ ($∵$ Area is symmetrical about $x -$~axis)

where ${x}_{1} = \dfrac{y^{2} + 1}{2}$and ~${x}_{2} = \dfrac{y^{2} + 3}{4}$

$⇒ A = 2{∫}_{0}^{1}\$left(\dfrac{y^{2} + 3}{4} - \dfrac{y^{2} + 1}{2}\right)$dy$~$= $\dfrac{2}{4}{∫}_{0}^{1}\left($1 - y^{2}\right)dy$

$= $\dfrac{1}{2}{y - \dfrac{y3}{3}}_{0}^{1}~ ~$= $\dfrac{1}{2} \left[1 - $\dfrac{1}{3}\right]

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}sq.units.

$

questions.q: The area, enclosed by the curves $y = sinx + cosx$ and $y = | cosx - sinx |$ and the lines $x = 0, x = \dfrac{π}{2},$& is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given curves are& $y = sinx + cosx \text{ and } y = \left|cosx - sinx\right|$

${y}_{1} = \text{sin x} + \text{cos x} = \sqrt{2} \text\sin \left(\text{x} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)
${y}_{2} = $\sqrt{2} | \text\sin \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \text{x}\right) |
So, Required Area$= \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi4}\left(\left(\text{sin x} + \text{cos x}\right) - \left(\text{cos x} - \text{sin x}\right)\right)\text{dx} + \mathop{∫}_{\pi4}^{\pi2}\left(\left(\text{sin x} + \text{cos x}\right) - \left(\text{sin x} - \text{cos x}\right)\right)\text{dx}
$2{∫}_{0}^{\pi4}sinxdx + 2{∫}_{\pi4}^{\pi2}cosxdx$
$= 4 - 2$\sqrt{2} =$2$\sqrt{2} \left(\sqrt{2} -$1\right).

$

The given equations are,

$⇒ y^{2} = 4 \left(1 - y\right)$

$⇒ y^{2} + 4y - 4 = 0 ⇒ y = $2\sqrt{2} -$2$

$∴$ Required Area $= \mathop{∫}_{0}^{2\sqrt{2} -$2} \left[ \left($1 - y\right) - \dfrac{y^{2}}{4}\right]dx = {\left($y - \dfrac{y^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{y^{3}}{12}\right)}_{0}^{2\sqrt{2} -2}$

$= \left[\left($2\sqrt{2} -2\right) - \dfrac{{ \lleft(2\sqrt{2} -2\right)}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{ \lleft(2\sqrt{2} -2\right)}^{3}}{12} -0\right]$

$= $\$lleft(2\sqrt{2} -$2\right)\left[1 - \$left(\sqrt{2} -$1\right) - $\dfrac{{\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)}^{2}}{3}\right] = - \dfrac{10}{3} + \dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{3}

$⇒ - $\dfrac{10}{3} + \dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{3} =$==a\sqrt{2} +b ⇒ a = \dfrac{8}{3},b = - \dfrac{10}{3}$
$∴ a - b = \dfrac{8}{3} + \dfrac{10}{3} =6$

$

questions.q: $Let $f: [ - 3, 1 ] \to R$ be given as~$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}min\left\{( x + 6 ) , x^{2}\right\}, & - 3 \le x \le 0 \\ max  \left\${\sqrt{x},$x^{2}\right\}, \text{ and } 0 ≤ x ≤ 1\end{cases} .\right$If the area bounded by $y = f ( x )$ and $x$-axis is $A$~sq units, then the value of $6A$ is equal to$

$⇒ x = 0 \text{ and } x = 1 .$

Hence, the area bounded by $y = f ( x )$ and $x$-axis is

$A = {∫}_{- 3}^{- 2} ( x + 6 ) dx + {∫}_{- 2}^{0}x^{2}dx + {∫}_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x}$dx$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,

$x - 2y + 4 \ge 0, x + 2y^{2} \ge 0, x + 4y^{2} \le 8, y \ge 0$

Now, finding the point of intersection of $x - 2y + 4 = 0 & x + 2y^{2} = 0$ we get,

\left(x, y\right) ≡ \left(-2, 1\right)$

And point of intersection of $x - 2y + 4 = 0 & x + 4y^{2} = 8$ will be, \left($x, y\right) ≡ \left(-1, $\dfrac{3}{2}\right)

Now, plotting the diagramw we get,

Now, from the above diagram, the required area will be,

$A = {∫}_{- 2}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x + 4}{2} - \sqrt{\dfrac{- x}{2}}\right) + {∫}_{- 1}^{0}\$left(\dfrac{8 - x}{2} - \sqrt{\dfrac{- x}{2}}\right)d x + {∫}_{0}^{8}\dfrac{8 - x}{2}$d x$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{1}{2}{\dfrac{\left(x + 4\right)2}{2}}_{- 2}^{- 1} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(- x\right)\dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{- 2}{3}\right)}_{- 2}^{- 1} + \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(8 - x\right)\dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{- 2}{3}\right)}_{- 1}^{0} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(- x\right)\dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{- 2}{3}\right)}_{- 1}^{0} + \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(8 - x\right)\dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{- 2}{3}\right)}_{0}^{8}$

$⇒ A = 9 + \dfrac{5}{4} - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{107}{12}$

$⇒ m + n = 119
